_doc: Asagiri Toru: the origin picked on the NEW GAME screen (docs/GDD.md 4.1, src/ui/toru_creator.gd) and his six stats (4.13, Toru autoload). Option fx: stats {stat: +n}, gain {stat|*: x} (stat gains), club_bonus {club|*: x}, job_bonus {job|*: x} (pay), money (+game units, 1 = 100 yen), money_set, flags [..], amane {bond_past|trust|self: +n}, tears_mult (his tears hit you harder: cold words shrink sooner), tones {tone|*: x} (Amane talk effects), calm (his tears fade x faster near you), jumpy, cats_mult (petting), sneeze, ghosts_early (minutes earlier for night spirits), lore, debt (game units every Sunday night), tokyo. mornings = lines that turn up at wake-up now and then. epilogue = the goal's last line on the end card ({when, text}, first match; when: min_stat, max_stat, min_money, ending, flag, route).

stat_desc.study: Exams, the newspaper and the council. Lessons, cram sessions, the library.
stat_desc.stamina: Shifts, practice, the 999 steps. Hard work costs it, sleep brings it back.
stat_desc.charm: How fast people warm up to you. Friends, customers, cats.
stat_desc.courage: The other side, the riverbed, saying no. Longer before the bell finds you in Ura-Suzunari.
stat_desc.agility: Running. Races, the relay, catching a cat with two tails.
stat_desc.transparency: What Toru wants: to be nobody. People start to forget you're there - teachers too. Amane never does.

categories.title: WHY HE WANTS TO BE INVISIBLE

options.name: Former child star
options.desc: At six you sang the Kitsune Udon jingle on national TV. You are seventeen now and strangers still finish the line for you.
mornings: A delivery man passes the house, does a double take and hums the Kitsune Udon jingle. You walk faster.
Two old ladies at the bus stop argue about whether you're 'that udon boy'. You are.
Haruka has taped your old commercial's poster inside the shop's back door. 'For luck,' she says. You turn it to face the wall.

options.name: The class turned its back
options.desc: In middle school one rumour went round and thirty people stopped seeing you. You learned to stop asking to be seen.
mornings: A notification from a group chat you left two years ago. You don't open it. You don't delete it either.
You dreamed of a classroom where every desk faced the wall. You woke up before yours did.

options.name: Burnt-out prodigy
options.desc: Top of every mock exam in Tokyo until one morning you couldn't open the book. Nobody asked why. You start clever and learn slowly.
mornings: Your old cram school sent a pamphlet: WE BELIEVE IN YOU (STILL). Haruka uses it as a coaster.
You solved this morning's newspaper puzzle in your head before the kettle boiled, and felt nothing at all.

options.name: In debt
options.desc: Your father's debts have your name on the second line. Every Sunday night ¥2,000 goes to Tokyo. You start with ¥3,000.
mornings: An envelope from a Tokyo loan office, addressed to you. Haruka slides it under the rice cooker without a word.
You count your coins before breakfast. It doesn't make more of them.

options.name: Just lazy
options.desc: No tragedy. People are tiring, and being nobody is restful.
mornings: You consider getting up. You consider it again. The alarm considers you back.
Haruka pulls your futon out from under you. 'Rise and shine, sloth.' You roll onto the tatami and keep sleeping.

options.name: Kind
options.desc: You pretend not to care, and then you carry everyone's bags. Kind words land harder.

options.name: Sharp-tongued
options.desc: Every kind thought leaves your mouth as a sarcastic one. Teasing and cold words land harder; kind ones less.

options.name: Indifferent
options.desc: Nothing reaches you. You've practised this face in mirrors. Everything you say to him lands softer.

options.name: Soft-hearted
options.desc: You can't watch anyone cry, not even in commercials. His tears hit you x1.5: cold words shrink sooner and further.

options.name: Calm
options.desc: Rain, ghosts, a crying boy on your doorstep: you breathe out and deal with it. His tears dry faster around you.

options.name: Jumpy
options.desc: Everything startles you. Especially someone peeking at you from behind a pillar.

options.name: Cooking
options.desc: Grandpa taught you tamagoyaki. It's the one thing you do well on purpose. Cooking Club and Asagiri-do go better.

options.name: Piano
options.desc: Eight years of lessons, then you closed the lid. Your hands still remember. Music Club goes better.

options.name: Karate
options.desc: Brown belt from a dojo above a pachinko parlour. You quit before the black one, like everything. Kendo and Track go better.

options.name: Drawing
options.desc: Margins full of cats. Your notebooks are half lessons, half sketches. Newspaper and Occult go better.

options.name: Games
options.desc: Rank 3 nationally in a rhythm game nobody plays any more. Fast hands; the konbini till loves you.

options.name: Nothing at all
options.desc: You never found it. Maybe this town has it. You learn everything a little faster.

options.name: Allergic to cats
options.desc: In a town of cats. You sneeze whenever one gets close, and they all come close. Petting works half as well.
mornings: Achoo. There is a cat on your windowsill. There is always a cat on your windowsill.
You took an allergy pill with breakfast. Outside, eight cats are waiting by the door like a welcome committee.

options.name: Sees ghosts
options.desc: Since you were small. You learned not to look twice. Night spirits show themselves to you an hour early.
mornings: The little girl at the end of the street waved again. She has been seven years old since you were seven.
Someone in an old school uniform was sitting on your desk when you woke up. You said 'good morning'. They left politely.

options.name: A girlfriend in Tokyo
options.desc: Saki. Long distance. She calls on Sunday nights. Mostly. Amane will find out.
mornings: A text from Saki: a photo of a Tokyo parfait, no words. You reply with a photo of rain. She doesn't reply.

options.name: Completely broke
options.desc: Wallet: one ¥5 coin for luck and a receipt. You start with nothing and work a little harder for it.
mornings: Breakfast is Haruka's leftover dango. Lunch, if you're lucky, will also be Haruka's leftover dango.

options.name: Former delinquent
options.desc: Bleached hair, a fight a week, a reputation in a town far away. You grew it out. The courage stayed.
mornings: Your knuckles ache when it rains. In Suzunari, that's every morning.

options.name: Remembers a little
options.desc: Rain on a muddy hill. The smell of rice. A bell. You don't know whose memories they are. Amane does.
mornings: You woke up counting steps. Nine hundred and ninety-eight, nine hundred and ninety-nine... and then a bell.
Your hands smelled of rice straw when you woke. You have never touched rice straw.

options.name: Pass the Tokyo University exam
options.desc: Your father's one condition for letting you come home. Study gains x1.25.

epilogue.text: Two winters later, Asagiri Toru passed the Tokyo University entrance exam. He took the train back to Suzunari the same night.
Asagiri Toru failed the Tokyo University exam by eleven points and enrolled at the prefectural university by the sea. He did not mind as much as he expected.
Asagiri Toru never sat the Tokyo University exam. His father stopped asking. Somewhere in a drawer, the application is still blank.

options.name: An ordinary girlfriend
options.desc: Someone normal. Movies, parfaits, no supernatural anything. Charm gains x1.25.

epilogue.text: Asagiri Toru wanted an ordinary girlfriend. He got a crying first-year with cat ears and a two-tailed shadow. Not ordinary. Not a girlfriend. He stopped minding.
Asagiri Toru went on four ordinary dates that summer. They were all very nice. He thought about rain the whole time.
Asagiri Toru is still looking for an ordinary girlfriend. Suzunari keeps not having one.

options.name: Save money and run away
options.desc: ¥150,000 and a train ticket to anywhere. Part-time pay x1.2.

epilogue.text: Asagiri Toru saved ¥150,000 by Tanabata. He bought a ticket to Sapporo, sat on the platform until the last train left, and walked home.
Asagiri Toru saved half of what he needed to run away. He spent it on a new umbrella for someone who cries too much.
Asagiri Toru never saved enough to run away. The town made sure of that, gently, one ten-yen coin at a time.

options.name: Do what the will says
options.desc: Grandpa Genzo's will, one line long: 'Climb the steps. Say what I never said.'

epilogue.text: At the thousandth step Asagiri Toru said the words his grandfather never said. Somewhere, a bell that had been silent since 1890 rang once.
Asagiri Toru understood the will by the end. He just wasn't ready to climb that last step. Not yet.
Asagiri Toru read the will every night and never understood it. The steps are still waiting.

options.name: Solve Grandpa's secret
options.desc: Why your father forbade Suzunari. Why Grandpa counted the steps. Why the cats bow to you.

epilogue.text: Asagiri Toru filled a whole notebook with his grandfather's secret. The last page just says: 'He kept a promise for 150 years. I'll keep it too.'
Asagiri Toru learned half of his grandfather's secret. The other half is in a box in Kiku's room, and Kiku isn't telling. Yet.
Asagiri Toru never solved his grandfather's secret. Grandpa, wherever he is, is probably relieved.

quirks._doc: Earned by how you live (checked every night). Effects are wired in code (Toru.quirk(id)).

escapist.name: Good at running away
escapist.desc: +30 s before the bell finds you in Ura-Suzunari.

cat_servant.name: Servant of cats
cat_servant.desc: Cats never go and tell Amane about you.

see_through.name: See-through
see_through.desc: People start to forget you're there: closeness grows slower, teachers forget to mark you absent. Amane always sees you.

third_eye.name: Third eye
third_eye.desc: Night spirits show themselves an hour early, and Ura's bell waits a little longer.

promise_breaker.name: Promise breaker
promise_breaker.desc: Doors open less often when you ring. Kotodama remembers.

tokyo_call.text: Sunday night. Your phone lights up: SAKI (TOKYO). Outside your window, very close, something with two tails stops moving.

choices.say: Saki talks about a new cafe for twenty minutes. You say 'mm' nineteen times. When you hang up, the rain has started.
A long silence from Tokyo. Then: 'Yeah. You've been somewhere else for months, Toru.' The line goes quiet. Outside, the rain stops all at once.
It rings eleven times. Then a text: 'ok.' The window is empty now.
